column1: # Cosimo's 35 cipher runs in Codex 533 (readings/runs_533.tsv), word by word, with the status that decides whether a
# word is counted as sure (recount of 15 Nov 2026, after Daniel Bourdeau's review of PR #665).
# Rule (README Conventions, "A reading must read" and "Holes are counted by words"): a word is SURE when every letter
# comes from frozen key v3 (key/key_v3.json) read on the signs as transcribed (a sign reading marked * in
# runs_533.tsv, e.g. 9 read as 5, is a transcription reading and is allowed), with no context-only value, no letter
# supplied or replaced by sense, no doubt mark and no unread group.
# status: sure; context = sure but for a context-only value (ww = o or 62 = q, key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md);
# supplied = a letter supplied where the cipher has nothing, or replaced by sense (README: a hole);
# context+supplied = both; doubtful = marked (?) or conjecture; hole N = unread, guessed or code number, N words (default 1).
# Words are as in the italian column of runs_533.tsv; "l'Elettore" is one word.
# Totals: 87 words. Sure 29 of 87 (33.3%). Sure or context-only value 41 of 87 (47.1%).
# Recount of 27 Nov 2026: L35 35r a "della" moved from sure to supplied, by this file's own rule (its four groups give
# d e l a, so the second l is supplied); before it, Sure 30 of 87 (34.5%), 42 of 87 (48.3%), Supplied 7.
# Daniel Bourdeau's count (review of PR #665): 37 of 87 sure, 51 of 87 with the context-only values. The 8-word
# difference is the eight 'supplied' words, which his count admits and README Conventions counts as holes; with them
# the two figures are 37 and 51 (the 51 adds permission[e] and sodisfatt[i]; ult[i]mo(?) stays out as doubtful).
